resources.string: Shorts Blocker reads the screen layout of the YouTube app only, to notice when the Shorts player opens, and presses Back for you. It does not read any other app, does not record what you watch, and has no internet access, so nothing leaves your phone.

1. Tap the button below.
2. Find "Shorts Blocker" (it may be under "Installed apps" or "Downloaded apps").
3. Turn it ON and tap Allow.
4. Come back here.

Is the switch greyed out, or does it say \"Restricted setting\"? Android does this for apps installed outside the Play Store. Tap below, then tap the ⋮ menu in the top corner → \"Allow restricted settings\", and try again.

Shorts Blocker uses Android's Accessibility permission to:

• Read the screen layout of the YouTube app only (not the video, not other apps)
• Notice when the Shorts player opens
• Press Back for you

It stores only a daily count of blocks. It has no internet access, so nothing you watch ever leaves your phone.
Find \"Shorts Blocker\" and turn it on
Open Settings → Accessibility and turn on Shorts Blocker
Finish the one-time setup above to start blocking.
Shorts are blocked on YouTube. Normal videos work as usual.
Blocking comes back on in about %1$d min.
Take a breath. You can choose in %1$d seconds…
No account. No internet. Nothing leaves your phone.
